data.why: the app loads examples/synthetic_sites.csv by default and accepts an uploaded CSV in the same schema, so the repo's own example plus a hand-written CSV covering a tight-margin/high-attention site, a zero-uncertainty boundary site, and a wide-uncertainty outlier site exercise the upload path and the attention-indicator logic.

goals: screen a batch of conceptual CO2 storage sites and compare their Q10/Q50/Q90 capacity estimates
inspect which uncertain input (area, thickness, porosity, density, efficiency) drives capacity uncertainty for a given site via the sensitivity chart
identify which sites warrant further investigation using the transparent containment-attention score and its components
upload a custom set of site scenarios and rerun the Monte Carlo simulation with a chosen sample count and seed
export the screening summary as a CSV for a given run

review.summary: The tree describes BasinLens's real purpose well: uncertainty-propagated volumetric capacity screening, kept separate from transparent containment-attention flags. Its phases and features match the small Streamlit app closely, and most cited screens are accurate. It needs light fixes before filing: two download actions cite a screen that doesn't show them, the global methodology task sits in the per-site phase, and preparing input data and the validation-error path are missing.
